subject: english
question:
**Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:**

The CEO is known to have been influenced by external advisors.

options.text: External advisors are known to influence the CEO.
Someone knew the CEO was influenced by external advisors.
People know that the CEO was influenced by external advisors.
External advisors are said to have influenced the CEO.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence "The CEO is known to have been influenced..." uses a **passive reporting verb** ("is known") followed by a **perfect passive infinitive** ("to have been influenced").
 
• To convert this to active voice, we must introduce a generic subject like "People" or "They" to perform the act of "knowing."
 
• The phrase "is known" (present tense) becomes "People know" or "They know."
 
• The perfect infinitive "to have been influenced" indicates an action that happened in the past. In an active "that-clause," this becomes "that the CEO **was influenced**" or "has been influenced."
 
• "People know that the CEO was influenced by external advisors" correctly maintains the present state of knowledge about a past influence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"People know that the CEO was influenced by external advisors."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "External advisors are known to influence..." changes the tense of the influence to the general present, losing the "have been" (past/completed) aspect.
 
• **Option 2:** "Someone knew..." changes the reporting verb to the past tense, which contradicts the original "is known" (present).
 
• **Option 4:** "External advisors are said to..." changes the meaning of the verb from "known" to "said," and remains in a passive-style construction.
